title: [RPG Design Guides] Turning Points in a Story

blocks.source: 【RPG制作講座】物語の転換点
blocks.translation: [RPG Design Guides] Turning Points in a Story

blocks.source: 起承転結の『転』――物語の転換点について考察してみる。
blocks.translation: Let’s examine the “ten”—the turning point—in kishotenketsu.

blocks.source: ここで言う転とは、主に物語の目的が転換するポイントを指す。例えば「魔王を倒したら、それを影で操る大魔王が現れた」などが典型だ。
blocks.translation: Here, “ten” mainly refers to the point where the story’s objective changes. A typical example would be, “After defeating the Demon King, the Great Demon King who had been controlling him from the shadows appears.”

blocks.source: 物語が根底から覆るような衝撃的な変化をした場合は『どんでん返し』なんて言葉でも呼ばれる。ストーリー制作者なら、一度は憧れた方も多いのではないだろうか。
blocks.translation: When a story undergoes a shocking change that overturns it from the ground up, it is also called a “plot twist.” Many story creators have probably dreamed of creating one at least once.

blocks.source: 目的自体が変化しなくとも、動機や手段に大きな変化をもたらすイベントも転換点となる。例えば、主人公の出生の秘密が明らかになることによって、大きな葛藤が発生するといった展開である。
blocks.translation: Even if the objective itself does not change, an event that greatly alters the motivation or means can also serve as a turning point. For example, the revelation of the protagonist’s secret birth might create a major internal conflict.

blocks.source: 転は物語半ばの山場である。長い物語をプレイヤーに飽きさせないために、重要な役割を果たす。
blocks.translation: The ten is the climax in the middle of the story. It plays an important role in keeping players from getting bored with a long story.

blocks.source: 物語の評価において「起承転結が弱い」なんて言われる作品は大抵の場合、転が弱いことを意味する。
blocks.translation: When a work is criticized for having a “weak kishotenketsu,” it usually means that its ten is weak.

blocks.source: 転は１つである必要はない。『起承転承転結』というように複数回の転を作ることも有効である。
blocks.translation: There does not have to be only one ten. Creating multiple turning points, such as in “ki-sho-ten-sho-ten-ketsu,” can also be effective.

blocks.source: ……そもそも、起承転結は元々は漢詩の構成法らしいので、長編ＲＰＧにそのまま適用するのは無理があったりする。
blocks.translation: …Actually, kishotenketsu was originally a structure for Chinese poetry, so applying it directly to a long RPG may not always work.

blocks.source: 特に長編になればなるほど、複数回の転が欲しくなってくる。
blocks.translation: The longer the story, in particular, the more you will want to include multiple turning points.

blocks.source: 例えば、長い長い中盤に全く転がないドラクエ７は中だるみするゲームとして有名だ。そうならないためにも、転を中心として全体の構成を考えてみたい。
blocks.translation: For example, Dragon Quest VII is famous as a game with a long, long middle section and no turning point at all, causing the pacing to drag. To avoid that, I would like to consider the overall structure with the turning points at its center.

blocks.source: 目次
blocks.translation: Table of Contents

blocks.source: 転を作ろう
blocks.translation: Creating a Turning Point

blocks.source: 転は起承転結の中でも比較的難易度が高い。
blocks.translation: The ten is relatively difficult to create compared with the other elements of kishotenketsu.

blocks.source: というのも『起承結』の三つは物語の最低限の構成要素であって、それなしではそもそも物語の成立は困難である。
blocks.translation: That is because the other three elements—ki, sho, and ketsu—are the minimum components of a story, and it is difficult for a story to exist without them in the first place.

blocks.source: どんな初心者でも物語の完成までたどり着けたならば、『起承結』は盛り込まれているのが普通だろう。
blocks.translation: If even a complete beginner manages to finish a story, it will ordinarily include ki, sho, and ketsu.

blocks.source: 対して、転はなくとも一応の物語が成立してしまう。ゆえに、初心者と上級者の実力差が強く出る部分だと言える。
blocks.translation: By contrast, a story can still be completed without a ten. For that reason, this is an area where the difference in ability between beginners and experts really shows.

blocks.source: しかしだからこそ、不慣れであっても転を意識して作ることに挑戦して欲しい。難しいからこそ、経験を積むことが重要となる。
blocks.translation: But that is precisely why I want you to challenge yourself to consciously create a turning point, even if you are inexperienced. The more difficult it is, the more important it becomes to gain experience.

blocks.source: 実際に転となる部分を考えてみると、
blocks.translation: When you actually try to think of a turning point,

blocks.source: 「こいつが黒幕なのはバレバレじゃないだろうか？」
blocks.translation: “Isn’t it completely obvious that this guy is the mastermind?”

blocks.source: 「この展開はありがちじゃないだろうか？」
blocks.translation: “Isn’t this development a cliché?”

blocks.source: などと不安になってくるかもしれない。
blocks.translation: You may start to worry about things like that.

blocks.source: 個人的にはそれでもないよりはマシだと思う。
blocks.translation: Personally, I think that even so, it is better than having no turning point at all.

blocks.source: たとえ、ありがちだったとしても、平坦なまま物語を終えるよりは強い印象を与えられるからだ。
blocks.translation: Even if it is clichéd, it can leave a stronger impression than ending the story on a flat note.

blocks.source: 必ずしも、ミステリー作家のような秀逸などんでん返しである必要はないし、プレイヤーが見たこともないような奇想天外なものである必要もない。
blocks.translation: It does not have to be an ingenious plot twist worthy of a mystery writer, nor does it have to be something utterly outlandish that players have never seen before.

blocks.source: まずはベタな展開でもよいから流れを変えてみよう。試してみれば、それだけで物語が引き締まってくるのが実感できると思う。
blocks.translation: First, try changing the direction of the story, even if the development is a cliché. Once you try it, I think you will be able to feel how the story becomes tighter simply as a result.

blocks.source: 転と起
blocks.translation: The Ten and the Ki

blocks.source: 実は起承転結の『起』も『転』と似たような特徴を持っている。
blocks.translation: In fact, the “ki” in kishotenketsu has characteristics similar to those of the “ten.”

blocks.source: 『起』とは大抵の場合、『平常からの転換』なのだから当然といえば当然。冒頭に『転』を持ってくれば『起』になるというわけだ。
blocks.translation: In most cases, “ki” means “a shift from the ordinary,” so this makes sense. Putting a “ten” at the beginning turns it into the “ki.”

blocks.source: よって『転』について考えることは『起』の参考にもなるかもしれない。
blocks.translation: Therefore, thinking about the “ten” may also provide ideas for the “ki.”

blocks.source: 転の例
blocks.translation: Examples of Turning Points

blocks.source: というわけで、転の例を挙げてみたい。
blocks.translation: So, I would like to give some examples of turning points.

blocks.source: これを見れば僕のような発想力の乏しい貧弱一般人でも、一応の『転』を作れるようになる……はず。
blocks.translation: If you read these, even an ordinary, unimaginative person like me should be able to create a passable “ten” …hopefully.

blocks.source: 前述の通り、転とは主に物語の目的の転換である。それを具体化するところから始めてみたい。
blocks.translation: As mentioned earlier, a ten is primarily a change in the story’s objective. I would like to start by making that more concrete.

blocks.source: よくある目的は『宿敵』に関わるものだ。
blocks.translation: A common type of objective involves a “ nemesis.”

blocks.source: ここでいう『宿敵』とは単なるライバルキャラではなく、物語の目的に直結する敵――ラスボスまたはそれに準ずる敵のことである。
blocks.translation: The “nemesis” referred to here is not merely a rival character, but an enemy directly connected to the story’s objective—the final boss or an equivalent enemy.

blocks.source: 例えば、ＤＱ３のバラモスやＤＱ６のムドーのような『偽のラスボス』もここには含まれる。
blocks.translation: This also includes “false final bosses,” such as Baramos in Dragon Quest III and Mudo in Dragon Quest VI.

blocks.source: 目的の達成
blocks.translation: Achieving the Objective

blocks.source: 目的の達成は物語の転換点になる。ゲーム中盤に大きな目的を達成して、次なる展開に進むというＲＰＧはよく見かけると思う。
blocks.translation: Achieving an objective becomes a turning point in the story. You have probably seen plenty of RPGs where the player achieves a major objective in the middle of the game and proceeds to the next development.

blocks.source: 最も王道なのは『宿敵との決着』である。
blocks.translation: The most classic example is “settling things with the nemesis.”

blocks.source: 大抵の場合は下の『新たな目的の登場』へと続く。……というか、そうでないと物語が終わってしまう。
blocks.translation: In most cases, this leads to the “emergence of a new objective” below. …Actually, without that, the story would end.

blocks.source: 新たな目的の登場
blocks.translation: The Emergence of a New Objective

blocks.source: 目的を達成した後も物語を続けたい場合は、新たな目的が必要となる。
blocks.translation: If you want the story to continue after the objective has been achieved, you need a new objective.

blocks.source: 次なる目標をプレイヤーに掲示しよう。
blocks.translation: Present the player with the next goal.

blocks.source: 代表的なのはやはり『新たな宿敵の登場』だろう。
blocks.translation: The most common example is probably “the appearance of a new nemesis.”

blocks.source: 「魔王を倒したら、それを影で操る大魔王が現れた」というような流れは定番。
blocks.translation: The kind of development where “after defeating the Demon King, the Great Demon King who had been controlling him from the shadows appears” is a classic.

blocks.source: 他にも、重要人物が裏切って新たな敵となるパターンは、最もどんでん返しらしいどんでん返しである。
blocks.translation: Another pattern is for an important character to betray the heroes and become a new enemy. This is probably the most quintessential kind of plot twist.

blocks.source: ラスボスの確定は転によって行われることが多い。
blocks.translation: The final boss is often established through a turning point.

blocks.source: 印象的な『ラスボス確定演出』ができれば、それだけで全体のストーリーも印象的になる。ぜひとも狙ってみるとよいだろう。
blocks.translation: If you can create an impressive “final boss reveal,” the entire story will become more memorable as a result. It is definitely worth aiming for.

blocks.source: 目的の明確化
blocks.translation: Clarifying the Objective

blocks.source: 物語の目的が明確化される。
blocks.translation: The story's objective becomes clear.

blocks.source: こちらは途中まで大きな目標を示さなかった場合、もしくは明確に示さなかった場合を前提としている。
blocks.translation: This assumes that no major goal was presented until this point, or that it was not presented clearly.

blocks.source: 目的の明確化は、起承転結の『起』でやることも多いのだが、実際には例外もある。
blocks.translation: The objective is often clarified in the “introduction” of the kishōtenketsu structure, but there are exceptions in practice.

blocks.source: 例えば、ＤＱ５の序盤に当たる少年期では、主人公は父に従う形で旅をする。その間、主人公自身は大きな目的を持つことはない。
blocks.translation: For example, during the protagonist's childhood period at the beginning of DQ5, he travels alongside his father. During this time, the protagonist himself has no major goal.

blocks.source: その後、父の遺言によって「母を探す」という目的が明確化される。
blocks.translation: Later, his father's dying words make his goal of “searching for his mother” clear.

blocks.source: その他には宿敵が明確になる場合などがある。
blocks.translation: Another possibility is for the archenemy to be revealed.

blocks.source: 今まで存在をつかめなかった悪の組織の首領が、ついに正体を現すようなパターンだ。
blocks.translation: For example, the leader of an evil organization whose existence had remained unknown finally reveals their identity.

blocks.source: 目的の変化
blocks.translation: Changes to the Objective

blocks.source: 目的を達成しない段階で、目的が変化してしまうパターン。
blocks.translation: This is the pattern in which the objective changes before it is achieved.

blocks.source: 例えば『宿敵』が部下の裏切りによって、死亡するパターンが挙げられる。多くの場合は、そのまま部下がラスボスとして君臨する。
blocks.translation: For example, the “archenemy” may be killed after being betrayed by a subordinate. In many cases, that subordinate then takes over as the final boss.

blocks.source: いわゆる下剋上型のラスボスである。
blocks.translation: This is the so-called usurper-type final boss.

blocks.source: あるいは、もっと大がかりなどんでん返しもあり得る。
blocks.translation: Alternatively, there may be an even more elaborate plot twist.

blocks.source: 今まで敵だと思っていた人物が正義の味方で、本来の敵は別にいたことが明らかになるなど。
blocks.translation: For instance, it may be revealed that the person thought to be an enemy was actually on the side of justice, and that the true enemy was someone else.

blocks.source: 目的の難化
blocks.translation: Complicating the Objective

blocks.source: 大まかな目的は変わらないまでも、それが難化するというパターン。
blocks.translation: This is the pattern in which the broad objective remains unchanged, but becomes more difficult.

blocks.source: 代表的なところでは敵の復活イベントだろうか。
blocks.translation: A typical example would be an event involving the enemy's resurrection.

blocks.source: 「主人公達の奔走は報われず、邪神の復活を許してしまう」とかそんな感じ。
blocks.translation: Something like, “The protagonists' efforts come to nothing, and they allow the evil god to be resurrected.”

blocks.source: これにより「邪神の復活を阻止」するという目的が「邪神の封印・討伐」へと格上げされる。
blocks.translation: As a result, the objective of “preventing the evil god's resurrection” is elevated to “sealing away or defeating the evil god.”

blocks.source: まあ、邪神の復活が阻止されたら、物語にならないし仕方ないね。
blocks.translation: Well, if the evil god's resurrection were prevented, there would be no story, so it can't be helped.

blocks.source: 他にも、宿敵のパワーアップイベントなどもそうだろう。
blocks.translation: An event in which the archenemy powers up would be another example.

blocks.source: なるべく劇的なパワーアップイベントを作ろう。
blocks.translation: Try to create a power-up event that is as dramatic as possible.

blocks.source: 「封印されし力を得た」とかそんな感じである。
blocks.translation: Something like, “He obtained a sealed power.”

blocks.source: 「ちょっと修行したら強くなった」だけではさすがに転とは言い難い。
blocks.translation: Simply saying, “He became stronger after training for a while,” would hardly qualify as a turning point.

blocks.source: ついでに破壊イベントや強制敗北イベントを作ってみてもよい。
blocks.translation: You could also try creating a destruction event or a forced defeat event.

blocks.source: 破壊イベントとは、力を手に入れた敵が町を見せしめに破壊したりするアレである。
blocks.translation: A destruction event is the sort of thing where an enemy who has gained power destroys a town as a warning to others.

blocks.source: 他にも最強と思っていた師匠キャラが、パワーアップした敵に殺されてしまうなんてのも定番だろう。
blocks.translation: Another classic example is when a mentor character thought to be invincible is killed by a powered-up enemy.

blocks.source: 物理的に強くなるだけでもよいが、他にも色々と考えられる。
blocks.translation: The character only needs to become physically stronger, but there are many other possibilities to consider.

blocks.source: 主人公は父の仇を討つために、大国の軍人である男を追う。
blocks.translation: The protagonist pursues a man who is a soldier of a great power in order to avenge his father's death.

blocks.source: 旅の末、大国にたどり着いたはいいが、男は大国の王になっていた。
blocks.translation: After a long journey, the protagonist finally reaches the great power, only to discover that the man has become its king.

blocks.source: 男を倒すには、大国そのものと戦う覚悟が必要となる。
blocks.translation: To defeat the man, the protagonist must be prepared to fight the great power itself.

blocks.source: 主人公は大国と戦う反乱軍に身を投じることに。
blocks.translation: The protagonist joins the rebel army fighting against the great power.

blocks.source: 目的の難化に伴い、「個人的な復讐劇」が「国家的な騒乱劇」に格上げされたことに注目して欲しい。
blocks.translation: Note how, as the objective becomes more difficult, the “personal revenge story” is elevated into a “national upheaval story.”

blocks.source: このように『目的の難化』には物語の流れを変える効果もある。
blocks.translation: In this way, “complicating the objective” can also change the flow of the story.

blocks.source: 目的に対する手段の変化
blocks.translation: Changes in the Means of Achieving the Objective

blocks.source: 大きな目的は変わらないが、手段や中期的な目的が変化する場合。
blocks.translation: This occurs when the major objective remains unchanged, but the means of achieving it or the intermediate objectives change.

blocks.source: これも立派な転換点である。
blocks.translation: This too is a significant turning point.

blocks.source: どのような時に手段が変化するかは、下記の『目的の失敗』や『目的に関する新事実』を見ていただければ。
blocks.translation: For examples of when the means change, see “Failure of the Objective” and “New Facts About the Objective” below.

blocks.source: 目的の失敗
blocks.translation: Failure of the Objective

blocks.source: 目的に挑んで失敗する――これもまた転換点となる。
blocks.translation: Attempting and failing to achieve the objective—this too becomes a turning point.

blocks.source: 例えば、物語中盤で宿敵に挑むが、返り討ちに合うような展開だ。
blocks.translation: For example, the protagonists may challenge the archenemy midway through the story, only to be defeated.

blocks.source: その後、宿敵を倒すための手段を探すといった展開に。
blocks.translation: The story then develops into a search for a way to defeat the archenemy.

blocks.source: あるいはその際に宿敵にヒロインをさらわれるなど、失敗の代償を払わされる展開にしてもよい。当面の目的はヒロインの救出になるわけだ。
blocks.translation: Alternatively, the failure could come at a cost, such as the archenemy abducting the heroine during the confrontation. The immediate objective then becomes rescuing the heroine.

blocks.source: ＳＦなら「地球に衝突する隕石を阻止するためにロケット兵器を打ち上げるが、破壊に失敗した」など、色々と考えられる。
blocks.translation: In science fiction, you could come up with ideas such as, “They launch a rocket weapon to stop a meteor from colliding with Earth, but fail to destroy it.”

blocks.source: 目的に関する新事実
blocks.translation: New Facts About the Objective

blocks.source: 宿敵の正体は主人公の父だった！
blocks.translation: The archenemy was the protagonist's father!

blocks.source: 敵を倒すためには、大きな犠牲を払う必要がある。
blocks.translation: Defeating the enemy requires making a great sacrifice.

blocks.source: ……というような展開。
blocks.translation: …That sort of development.

blocks.source: 上の例はＦＦ１０だが、「宿敵の正体」「倒すために必要な代償」などが掲示された結果、主人公にとって目的を達成する意味合いが大きく変化してくる。その結果、手段の変更も決意することになる。
blocks.translation: The example above is from Final Fantasy X, but once facts such as “the archenemy's identity” and “the sacrifice required to defeat them” are revealed, the significance of achieving the objective changes greatly for the protagonist. As a result, the protagonist also decides to change their means of achieving it.

blocks.source: ただし、敵を倒すという目的自体は当初から変化していない。
blocks.translation: However, the objective of defeating the enemy itself has not changed from the beginning.

blocks.source: 他にも「悪だと思っていた敵にも、同情できる事情があった」なんていう王道パターンもこれである。
blocks.translation: Another classic example is when “even the enemy thought to be evil had circumstances that made them sympathetic.”

blocks.source: 転を強調しよう
blocks.translation: Let's Emphasize the Turning Point

blocks.source: さらに具体的に転を強調する方法を考えてみよう。
blocks.translation: Let's consider some more specific ways to emphasize the turning point.

blocks.source: 『主人公側に関わるもの』『世界・舞台に関わるもの』の二種類に分けてみる。これらが『目的の転換』に結びつくことで、印象的な転が生まれるというわけだ。
blocks.translation: Let's divide them into two types: “things involving the protagonist's side” and “things involving the world and setting.” When these lead to “a change of objective,” they create an impactful turning point.

blocks.source: 主人公側に関わるもの
blocks.translation: Things Involving the Protagonist's Side

blocks.source: 『転』においては主人公側に関わる出来事が多用される傾向がある。
blocks.translation: Events involving the protagonist's side tend to be used frequently in the “turning point” section.

blocks.source: 主人公やヒロイン、仲間に関わるイベントを起こすことで、印象的な転を作ろう。
blocks.translation: Create an impactful turning point by introducing events involving the protagonist, heroine, or companions.

blocks.source: 主人公の変更
blocks.translation: Changing the Protagonist

blocks.source: 主人公の変更。これはゲーム性への影響も大きな転換である。
blocks.translation: Changing the protagonist. This is also a major shift that greatly affects the gameplay.

blocks.source: 王道なのは主人公が死亡するなどして、その子世代に主人公が変更されることだろう。この場合は、時間経過と組み合わされることが多い。
blocks.translation: The classic example is for the protagonist to die or otherwise be replaced by their child in the next generation. This is often combined with the passage of time.

blocks.source: 主観視点の交代
blocks.translation: Changing the Point-of-View Character

blocks.source: 単純なところでは、章が変わって視点となるキャラが交代するなど。ただし、それだけでは転としては弱いかも。
blocks.translation: A simple example would be changing the point-of-view character when the chapter changes. However, that alone may be too weak to serve as a turning point.

blocks.source: 他にも主人公が危機的な状況に陥って、ヒロインなどの他のキャラが第二の主人公として動き出すなど。
blocks.translation: Another possibility is for the protagonist to fall into a critical situation, prompting another character, such as the heroine, to take action as a second protagonist.

blocks.source: 主人公の大きな決断
blocks.translation: The Protagonist's Major Decision

blocks.source: 物語の流れを大きく変えるような主人公の決断。
blocks.translation: A decision by the protagonist that dramatically changes the course of the story.

blocks.source: 所属組織からの脱退・離反
blocks.translation: Leaving or defecting from their organization

blocks.source: 悪事
blocks.translation: Committing an evil deed

blocks.source: などが代表例だろうか。
blocks.translation: These would be representative examples.

blocks.source: ストーリー上で強制しても良いし、もちろんプレイヤーに選択させてもよい。
blocks.translation: You can force the decision as part of the story, or, of course, let the player choose.

blocks.source: ＦＦ４の冒頭や、タクティクスオウガの一章終盤の選択肢などが有名だろう。
blocks.translation: The opening of FF4 and the choice near the end of Chapter One in Tactics Ogre are famous examples.

blocks.source: 仲間の離脱
blocks.translation: A Companion's Departure

blocks.source: 一時的にちょっと離脱するだけなら大したことはないが、死亡などの永久離脱は大きな衝撃になる。
blocks.translation: A brief, temporary departure is not a big deal, but a permanent departure, such as death, can be a major shock.

blocks.source: 時にはヒロインや主人公まで対象となったりする。
blocks.translation: Sometimes even the heroine or protagonist can be affected.

blocks.source: ＦＦ６のようにメンバー全員が離散するなんて展開も。
blocks.translation: There are also developments like in FF6, where all the members are scattered.

blocks.source: 重要人物の裏切り
blocks.translation: The Betrayal of an Important Character

blocks.source: 定番のどんでん返し。
blocks.translation: A classic plot twist.

blocks.source: そのまま仲間だった人物が宿敵になったり、もう一度復縁したりと展開は様々。
blocks.translation: The developments can vary: a former companion may become a sworn enemy, or the two may reconcile once again.

blocks.source: 重要人物の死亡
blocks.translation: The Death of an Important Character

blocks.source: 例えば、パワーアップしたラスボスに師匠キャラが殺害されるような展開があれば、ラスボスの印象が強まるだろう。
blocks.translation: For example, if a mentor character is killed by a powered-up final boss, it will make the final boss more memorable.

blocks.source: 宿敵と思っていた相手が黒幕に殺されるとか、主人公に指示を出していた組織の長が殺される――といった展開なら、物語の流れも変わってくる。
blocks.translation: If the person you thought was your sworn enemy is killed by the mastermind, or the leader of the organization directing the protagonist is killed, the course of the story will change as well.

blocks.source: 当然、どうでもいいキャラでは転換点にはならない。
blocks.translation: Naturally, the death of an insignificant character will not become a turning point.

blocks.source: 主人公やヒロインの秘密が明かされる
blocks.translation: The Protagonist's or Heroine's Secret Is Revealed

blocks.source: 実は王族だったとか、人間じゃなかったとかいうのが最もベタだが、やりようはいくらでもある。
blocks.translation: The most clichéd examples are that they were actually royalty or were not human, but there are countless ways to handle it.

blocks.source: それによって、新たな展開につながったりする。
blocks.translation: This can lead to new developments.

blocks.source: 協力者の登場
blocks.translation: The Appearance of an Ally

blocks.source: ネガティブな展開ばかりを書いている気がするけれど、ポジティブな展開も大事。
blocks.translation: I feel like I've been writing only negative developments, but positive developments are important too.

blocks.source: 協力者の登場によって、絶望的な状況に光明が見えてくる展開など。
blocks.translation: For example, the appearance of an ally can bring a glimmer of hope to a desperate situation.

blocks.source: 敵側の人物が改心して仲間になってくれるなども効果的だ。もしくは最初からスパイ的な活動をしていただけで、味方だったなどのパターンもある。
blocks.translation: It can also be effective for someone on the enemy's side to repent and join the party. Another possibility is that they were actually an ally all along, merely pretending to act as a spy.

blocks.source: 恋愛成就
blocks.translation: Romantic Success

blocks.source: 例えば、主人公がヒロインに告白して成功する――なんて展開も場合によっては立派なターニングポイントになる。
blocks.translation: For example, the protagonist confessing their love to the heroine and succeeding can, in some cases, be a significant turning point.

blocks.source: 悪の組織に追われるヒロインを守る――といった動機づけによって、ストーリー展開に大きな影響を与えることも。
blocks.translation: It can also have a major impact on the story's development by providing motivation such as protecting the heroine from an evil organization.

blocks.source: 中盤で結婚するＤＱ５なんかが有名。
blocks.translation: DQ5, in which the protagonist gets married midway through the game, is a famous example.

blocks.source: ただし、現代的な恋愛劇として見た場合は、圧倒的に描写が足りないのは玉に瑕。
blocks.translation: However, when viewed as a modern romance, its regrettable flaw is that it lacks an overwhelming amount of character development.

blocks.source: 逆に振られてしまう場合も立派に印象づけられるけれど、いささかマニアックなのは否めないし、某ラグーンぐらいしか有名作を知らない。
blocks.translation: Being rejected can also make a strong impression, but I have to admit that it is somewhat niche, and the only famous example I know is that certain Lagoon game.

blocks.source: 世界・舞台に関わるもの
blocks.translation: Things Involving the World and Setting

blocks.source: 物語の転換点においては、世界・舞台の変化が行われることも多い。
blocks.translation: Story turning points are also often accompanied by changes to the world or setting.

blocks.source: 世界・舞台の移動
blocks.translation: Moving to a Different World or Setting

blocks.source: 魔王が支配する暗黒の世界、雲の上の浮遊大陸、未知の生物が跋扈する地底……。こういった舞台への移動は、大作ＲＰＧの醍醐味である。
blocks.translation: A dark world ruled by a demon king, floating continents above the clouds, an underground realm teeming with unknown creatures... Moving to settings like these is one of the great pleasures of a large-scale RPG.

blocks.source: ＳＦならば宇宙船で新たな惑星に移動したり、タイムマシンで別の時代に移動したりすることもあるだろう。
blocks.translation: In science fiction, the characters may travel to a new planet by spaceship or to another era in a time machine.

blocks.source: 必ずしも、大規模な変化である必要はない。
blocks.translation: The change does not necessarily have to be on a grand scale.

blocks.source: ＦＦ７の序盤は、都市ミッドガルを舞台に物語が展開されるが、やがて世界を舞台にした物語へと広がっていく。これもまた舞台の移動である。
blocks.translation: In the early part of FF7, the story unfolds in the city of Midgar, but eventually expands into a story set across the world. This is also a change of setting.

blocks.source: 時間の経過
blocks.translation: The Passage of Time

blocks.source: 時間経過によって、物語を転換させる手法。
blocks.translation: A technique for shifting the story through the passage of time.

blocks.source: 有名なのはＤＱ５だろう。
blocks.translation: DQ5 is probably the most famous example.

blocks.source: 父に連れられていた少年時代から、自ら立って歩く青年時代へと主人公は成長を遂げる。
blocks.translation: The protagonist grows from a boy who was led around by his father into a young man who can stand and walk on his own.

blocks.source: さらに再度の時間経過によって、誕生した子供達が成長して戦いに参加するようになる。
blocks.translation: Then, after another passage of time, the children who were born grow up and join the battle.

blocks.source: 当然ながら、時間が経過すると世界中の住民も歳を取る。そういった住民の変化を実装するのは、なかなかの難作業である。
blocks.translation: Naturally, as time passes, the people throughout the world grow older as well. Implementing such changes among the inhabitants is quite a difficult task.

blocks.source: そう考えると、序盤の多くの町が登場していない段階で、しかけるのが無難なところか。
blocks.translation: With that in mind, it may be safest to introduce it before many towns appear in the early part of the story.

blocks.source: 実際、ごく序盤のイベントのみを少年期で行う作品も時々見かける。もっとも、これは『転』というより『起』寄りのような気がしないでもない。
blocks.translation: In fact, I occasionally see works in which only the very early events take place during the protagonist's childhood. Still, this feels closer to the "setup" than the "turn."

blocks.source: あるいは、一年程度の時間経過を導入する方法もある。
blocks.translation: Alternatively, you could introduce a passage of about one year.

blocks.source: こちらならば住民に大きな変化はないはずなので、セリフなどを変更しなくとも違和感はないはず。
blocks.translation: Since the inhabitants should not change much in that time, it should not feel strange even if you do not change their dialogue.

blocks.source: ただし、意味もなく時間経過を導入しても仕方ないので、何らかの変化は必要だが。
blocks.translation: However, introducing a passage of time without a purpose would be pointless, so some kind of change is necessary.

blocks.source: 舞台の破壊
blocks.translation: Destruction of the Setting

blocks.source: 町や国が破壊されたり、島や大陸が沈んだりする。
blocks.translation: Towns and countries are destroyed, or islands and continents sink beneath the sea.

blocks.source: あるいはＦＦ６のように世界まるごと大打撃を受けてもよい。
blocks.translation: Alternatively, the entire world could suffer a devastating blow, as in FF6.

blocks.source: これによって敵の強大さや凶悪さを印象づけたり、主人公側に動機づけを行ったりする。
blocks.translation: This can impress upon the player how powerful and ruthless the enemy is, or give the protagonist's side motivation to act.

blocks.source: 『起』でも『転』でも使えるイベント界の優等生。大規模にやると演出が大変になるのが玉に瑕。
blocks.translation: A model event that can be used for either the "setup" or the "turn." The drawback is that large-scale destruction can be difficult to stage.

blocks.source: とりあえず主人公の故郷を焼いたりするのは基本。
blocks.translation: Burning down the protagonist's hometown is a basic example.

blocks.source: 世界規模での異変
blocks.translation: A World-Scale Calamity

blocks.source: 世界が暗闇に覆われる。雨が永遠に止まらない。世界中の陸地が水没する。モンスターの大量発生。などなど……。
blocks.translation: The world is shrouded in darkness. The rain never stops. All the land in the world is submerged. Monsters appear in huge numbers. And so on…

blocks.source: 敵によって人為的に起こされたか、自然現象的なものなのかによって、また展開が変わってくる。
blocks.translation: The story will develop differently depending on whether the enemy caused it deliberately or whether it is a natural phenomenon.

blocks.source: 隕石を阻止するＦＦ７のように、それら天変地異の阻止が最終目的となる場合もある。
blocks.translation: In some cases, stopping such natural disasters becomes the ultimate goal, as in FF7, where the heroes must stop a meteor.

blocks.source: 「ラスボスを倒さないと世界がヤバい！」なんて文章を中心に説明する作品は多いけれど、それだけではイマイチ実感が湧かないもの。
blocks.translation: Many works center their explanations around lines such as, "The world is doomed unless we defeat the final boss!" But that alone does not make the threat feel very real.

blocks.source: 上の『舞台の破壊』もそうだけど、こうやって具体的な演出を入れると効果てきめんだ。
blocks.translation: The same applies to the "Destruction of the Setting" mentioned above, but adding concrete staging like this can be extremely effective.

blocks.source: 転の注意点
blocks.translation: Points to Keep in Mind About the Turn

blocks.source: ここまで熱烈に『転』を推してきたけど、転は万能ではない。強引に転をしかけた場合は、物語に対してマイナスに働く場合もある。
blocks.translation: I have strongly advocated the "turn" up to this point, but it is not a cure-all. If you force a turn into the story, it can also have a negative effect.

blocks.source: それはテーマがブレることである。
blocks.translation: That effect is a shift in the theme.

blocks.source: 例えば「主人公とライバルとの対決」というテーマが物語の全体の多くを占める作品だったとしよう。
blocks.translation: For example, suppose a work's overall story is largely devoted to the theme of "the protagonist's confrontation with their rival."

blocks.source: そこで終盤になって唐突に「黒幕の手によって、ライバルが殺害される」という転を導入するとどうなるだろうか？
blocks.translation: What would happen if, near the end, you suddenly introduced a turn in which "the rival is killed by the mastermind"?

blocks.source: これにより「主人公とライバルとの対決」というテーマが終わってしまうため、プレイヤーが興冷めしてしまう可能性は高いだろう。
blocks.translation: This would bring the theme of "the protagonist's confrontation with their rival" to an end, so there is a high chance that players would lose interest.

blocks.source: こういった場合も、なるべく自然なテーマの変化を目指そう。
blocks.translation: Even in such cases, aim for the theme to change as naturally as possible.

blocks.source: 例えば……
blocks.translation: For example…

blocks.source: 幾度の戦いの末、主人公とライバルはついに和解する。手段は違えど、二人とも世界の平和を目指す志は同じだったのだ。
blocks.translation: After countless battles, the protagonist and their rival finally reconcile. Although their methods differed, they shared the same aspiration to bring peace to the world.

blocks.source: だが、ライバルを影で利用していた黒幕は彼を殺害する。
blocks.translation: However, the mastermind who had been using the rival from the shadows kills him.

blocks.source: 世界征服を企む黒幕にとって、もはやライバルは邪魔でしかなかったのだ。
blocks.translation: To the mastermind plotting to conquer the world, the rival was no longer anything but an obstacle.

blocks.source: 主人公はライバルの目指した世界平和を目指すため、黒幕との最後の戦いに挑む。
blocks.translation: The protagonist challenges the mastermind to one final battle in order to pursue the world peace their rival had sought.

blocks.source: テーマが「ライバルとの対決」から「ライバルの遺志を継ぐ」に転換されたわけだが、これなら比較的違和感は少ないはず。
blocks.translation: The theme has shifted from "confronting the rival" to "carrying on the rival's will," which should feel relatively natural.

blocks.source: まとめ
blocks.translation: Conclusion

blocks.source: 以上、色々と例を挙げてみた。
blocks.translation: Those are some of the various examples I could think of.

blocks.source: 簡単にできるものから演出的に難しいものまであるけれど、色々と考えてみていただければ。
blocks.translation: Some are easy to implement, while others are difficult to stage, but I hope you will consider the possibilities.

blocks.source: なお、実際には複数の要素を組み合わせて『転』を演出することが多い。
blocks.translation: In practice, a "turn" is often created by combining multiple elements.

blocks.source: 例えば、ＦＦ６の中盤の転換点では、『目的の変化』『目的の難化』『目的の失敗』『舞台の破壊』『メンバーの離脱』『時間の経過』など数多くの要素が含まれている。
blocks.translation: For example, the turning point in the middle of FF6 includes many elements, such as "a change in objectives," "an increasingly difficult objective," "failure to achieve the objective," "destruction of the setting," "the departure of a party member," and "the passage of time."

blocks.source: 強い印象を与えたい場合は、上述の要素を柔軟に組み合わせてみて欲しい。もちろん、ここに挙がっていない方法の中にも、有効なものもあるかもしれない。
blocks.translation: If you want to make a strong impression, try combining the elements mentioned above flexibly. Of course, there may also be effective methods among those not listed here.

texts.起承転結の『転』――物語の転換点について考察してみる。: Let’s examine the “ten”—the turning point—in kishotenketsu.
texts.ここで言う転とは、主に物語の目的が転換するポイントを指す。例えば「魔王を倒したら: Here, “ten” mainly refers to the point where the story’s objective changes. A typical example would be, “After defeating the Demon King, the Great Demon King who had been controlling him from the shadows appears.”
texts.物語が根底から覆るような衝撃的な変化をした場合は『どんでん返し』なんて言葉でも呼: When a story undergoes a shocking change that overturns it from the ground up, it is also called a “plot twist.” Many story creators have probably dreamed of creating one at least once.
texts.目的自体が変化しなくとも、動機や手段に大きな変化をもたらすイベントも転換点となる: Even if the objective itself does not change, an event that greatly alters the motivation or means can also serve as a turning point. For example, the revelation of the protagonist’s secret birth might create a major internal conflict.
texts.転は物語半ばの山場である。長い物語をプレイヤーに飽きさせないために、重要な役割を: The ten is the climax in the middle of the story. It plays an important role in keeping players from getting bored with a long story.
texts.物語の評価において「起承転結が弱い」なんて言われる作品は大抵の場合、転が弱いこと: When a work is criticized for having a “weak kishotenketsu,” it usually means that its ten is weak.
texts.転は１つである必要はない。『起承転承転結』というように複数回の転を作ることも有効: There does not have to be only one ten. Creating multiple turning points, such as in “ki-sho-ten-sho-ten-ketsu,” can also be effective.
texts.……そもそも、起承転結は元々は漢詩の構成法らしいので、長編ＲＰＧにそのまま適用す: …Actually, kishotenketsu was originally a structure for Chinese poetry, so applying it directly to a long RPG may not always work.
texts.特に長編になればなるほど、複数回の転が欲しくなってくる。: The longer the story, in particular, the more you will want to include multiple turning points.
texts.例えば、長い長い中盤に全く転がないドラクエ７は中だるみするゲームとして有名だ。そ: For example, Dragon Quest VII is famous as a game with a long, long middle section and no turning point at all, causing the pacing to drag. To avoid that, I would like to consider the overall structure with the turning points at its center.
texts.転は起承転結の中でも比較的難易度が高い。: The ten is relatively difficult to create compared with the other elements of kishotenketsu.
texts.というのも『起承結』の三つは物語の最低限の構成要素であって、それなしではそもそも: That is because the other three elements—ki, sho, and ketsu—are the minimum components of a story, and it is difficult for a story to exist without them in the first place.
texts.どんな初心者でも物語の完成までたどり着けたならば、『起承結』は盛り込まれているの: If even a complete beginner manages to finish a story, it will ordinarily include ki, sho, and ketsu.
texts.対して、転はなくとも一応の物語が成立してしまう。ゆえに、初心者と上級者の実力差が: By contrast, a story can still be completed without a ten. For that reason, this is an area where the difference in ability between beginners and experts really shows.
texts.しかしだからこそ、不慣れであっても転を意識して作ることに挑戦して欲しい。難しいか: But that is precisely why I want you to challenge yourself to consciously create a turning point, even if you are inexperienced. The more difficult it is, the more important it becomes to gain experience.
texts.実際に転となる部分を考えてみると、: When you actually try to think of a turning point,
texts.「こいつが黒幕なのはバレバレじゃないだろうか？」: “Isn’t it completely obvious that this guy is the mastermind?”
texts.などと不安になってくるかもしれない。: You may start to worry about things like that.
texts.個人的にはそれでもないよりはマシだと思う。: Personally, I think that even so, it is better than having no turning point at all.
texts.たとえ、ありがちだったとしても、平坦なまま物語を終えるよりは強い印象を与えられる: Even if it is clichéd, it can leave a stronger impression than ending the story on a flat note.
texts.必ずしも、ミステリー作家のような秀逸などんでん返しである必要はないし、プレイヤー: It does not have to be an ingenious plot twist worthy of a mystery writer, nor does it have to be something utterly outlandish that players have never seen before.
texts.まずはベタな展開でもよいから流れを変えてみよう。試してみれば、それだけで物語が引: First, try changing the direction of the story, even if the development is a cliché. Once you try it, I think you will be able to feel how the story becomes tighter simply as a result.
texts.実は起承転結の『起』も『転』と似たような特徴を持っている。: In fact, the “ki” in kishotenketsu has characteristics similar to those of the “ten.”
texts.『起』とは大抵の場合、『平常からの転換』なのだから当然といえば当然。冒頭に『転』: In most cases, “ki” means “a shift from the ordinary,” so this makes sense. Putting a “ten” at the beginning turns it into the “ki.”
texts.よって『転』について考えることは『起』の参考にもなるかもしれない。: Therefore, thinking about the “ten” may also provide ideas for the “ki.”
texts.というわけで、転の例を挙げてみたい。: So, I would like to give some examples of turning points.
texts.これを見れば僕のような発想力の乏しい貧弱一般人でも、一応の『転』を作れるようにな: If you read these, even an ordinary, unimaginative person like me should be able to create a passable “ten” …hopefully.
texts.前述の通り、転とは主に物語の目的の転換である。それを具体化するところから始めてみ: As mentioned earlier, a ten is primarily a change in the story’s objective. I would like to start by making that more concrete.
texts.よくある目的は『宿敵』に関わるものだ。: A common type of objective involves a “ nemesis.”
texts.ここでいう『宿敵』とは単なるライバルキャラではなく、物語の目的に直結する敵――ラ: The “nemesis” referred to here is not merely a rival character, but an enemy directly connected to the story’s objective—the final boss or an equivalent enemy.
texts.例えば、ＤＱ３のバラモスやＤＱ６のムドーのような『偽のラスボス』もここには含まれ: This also includes “false final bosses,” such as Baramos in Dragon Quest III and Mudo in Dragon Quest VI.
texts.目的の達成は物語の転換点になる。ゲーム中盤に大きな目的を達成して、次なる展開に進: Achieving an objective becomes a turning point in the story. You have probably seen plenty of RPGs where the player achieves a major objective in the middle of the game and proceeds to the next development.
texts.最も王道なのは『宿敵との決着』である。: The most classic example is “settling things with the nemesis.”
texts.大抵の場合は下の『新たな目的の登場』へと続く。……というか、そうでないと物語が終: In most cases, this leads to the “emergence of a new objective” below. …Actually, without that, the story would end.
texts.新たな目的の登場: The Emergence of a New Objective
texts.目的を達成した後も物語を続けたい場合は、新たな目的が必要となる。: If you want the story to continue after the objective has been achieved, you need a new objective.
texts.次なる目標をプレイヤーに掲示しよう。: Present the player with the next goal.
texts.代表的なのはやはり『新たな宿敵の登場』だろう。: The most common example is probably “the appearance of a new nemesis.”
texts.「魔王を倒したら、それを影で操る大魔王が現れた」というような流れは定番。: The kind of development where “after defeating the Demon King, the Great Demon King who had been controlling him from the shadows appears” is a classic.
texts.他にも、重要人物が裏切って新たな敵となるパターンは、最もどんでん返しらしいどんで: Another pattern is for an important character to betray the heroes and become a new enemy. This is probably the most quintessential kind of plot twist.
texts.ラスボスの確定は転によって行われることが多い。: The final boss is often established through a turning point.
texts.印象的な『ラスボス確定演出』ができれば、それだけで全体のストーリーも印象的になる: If you can create an impressive “final boss reveal,” the entire story will become more memorable as a result. It is definitely worth aiming for.
texts.こちらは途中まで大きな目標を示さなかった場合、もしくは明確に示さなかった場合を前: This assumes that no major goal was presented until this point, or that it was not presented clearly.
texts.目的の明確化は、起承転結の『起』でやることも多いのだが、実際には例外もある。: The objective is often clarified in the “introduction” of the kishōtenketsu structure, but there are exceptions in practice.
texts.例えば、ＤＱ５の序盤に当たる少年期では、主人公は父に従う形で旅をする。その間、主: For example, during the protagonist's childhood period at the beginning of DQ5, he travels alongside his father. During this time, the protagonist himself has no major goal.
texts.その後、父の遺言によって「母を探す」という目的が明確化される。: Later, his father's dying words make his goal of “searching for his mother” clear.
texts.その他には宿敵が明確になる場合などがある。: Another possibility is for the archenemy to be revealed.
texts.今まで存在をつかめなかった悪の組織の首領が、ついに正体を現すようなパターンだ。: For example, the leader of an evil organization whose existence had remained unknown finally reveals their identity.
texts.目的を達成しない段階で、目的が変化してしまうパターン。: This is the pattern in which the objective changes before it is achieved.
texts.例えば『宿敵』が部下の裏切りによって、死亡するパターンが挙げられる。多くの場合は: For example, the “archenemy” may be killed after being betrayed by a subordinate. In many cases, that subordinate then takes over as the final boss.
texts.いわゆる下剋上型のラスボスである。: This is the so-called usurper-type final boss.
texts.あるいは、もっと大がかりなどんでん返しもあり得る。: Alternatively, there may be an even more elaborate plot twist.
texts.今まで敵だと思っていた人物が正義の味方で、本来の敵は別にいたことが明らかになるな: For instance, it may be revealed that the person thought to be an enemy was actually on the side of justice, and that the true enemy was someone else.
texts.大まかな目的は変わらないまでも、それが難化するというパターン。: This is the pattern in which the broad objective remains unchanged, but becomes more difficult.
texts.代表的なところでは敵の復活イベントだろうか。: A typical example would be an event involving the enemy's resurrection.
texts.「主人公達の奔走は報われず、邪神の復活を許してしまう」とかそんな感じ。: Something like, “The protagonists' efforts come to nothing, and they allow the evil god to be resurrected.”
texts.これにより「邪神の復活を阻止」するという目的が「邪神の封印・討伐」へと格上げされ: As a result, the objective of “preventing the evil god's resurrection” is elevated to “sealing away or defeating the evil god.”
texts.まあ、邪神の復活が阻止されたら、物語にならないし仕方ないね。: Well, if the evil god's resurrection were prevented, there would be no story, so it can't be helped.
texts.他にも、宿敵のパワーアップイベントなどもそうだろう。: An event in which the archenemy powers up would be another example.
texts.なるべく劇的なパワーアップイベントを作ろう。: Try to create a power-up event that is as dramatic as possible.
texts.「封印されし力を得た」とかそんな感じである。: Something like, “He obtained a sealed power.”
texts.「ちょっと修行したら強くなった」だけではさすがに転とは言い難い。: Simply saying, “He became stronger after training for a while,” would hardly qualify as a turning point.
texts.ついでに破壊イベントや強制敗北イベントを作ってみてもよい。: You could also try creating a destruction event or a forced defeat event.
texts.破壊イベントとは、力を手に入れた敵が町を見せしめに破壊したりするアレである。: A destruction event is the sort of thing where an enemy who has gained power destroys a town as a warning to others.
texts.他にも最強と思っていた師匠キャラが、パワーアップした敵に殺されてしまうなんてのも: Another classic example is when a mentor character thought to be invincible is killed by a powered-up enemy.
texts.物理的に強くなるだけでもよいが、他にも色々と考えられる。: The character only needs to become physically stronger, but there are many other possibilities to consider.
texts.主人公は父の仇を討つために、大国の軍人である男を追う。: The protagonist pursues a man who is a soldier of a great power in order to avenge his father's death.
texts.旅の末、大国にたどり着いたはいいが、男は大国の王になっていた。: After a long journey, the protagonist finally reaches the great power, only to discover that the man has become its king.
texts.男を倒すには、大国そのものと戦う覚悟が必要となる。: To defeat the man, the protagonist must be prepared to fight the great power itself.
texts.主人公は大国と戦う反乱軍に身を投じることに。: The protagonist joins the rebel army fighting against the great power.
texts.目的の難化に伴い、「個人的な復讐劇」が「国家的な騒乱劇」に格上げされたことに注目: Note how, as the objective becomes more difficult, the “personal revenge story” is elevated into a “national upheaval story.”
texts.このように『目的の難化』には物語の流れを変える効果もある。: In this way, “complicating the objective” can also change the flow of the story.
texts.目的に対する手段の変化: Changes in the Means of Achieving the Objective
texts.大きな目的は変わらないが、手段や中期的な目的が変化する場合。: This occurs when the major objective remains unchanged, but the means of achieving it or the intermediate objectives change.
texts.これも立派な転換点である。: This too is a significant turning point.
texts.どのような時に手段が変化するかは、下記の『目的の失敗』や『目的に関する新事実』を: For examples of when the means change, see “Failure of the Objective” and “New Facts About the Objective” below.
texts.目的に挑んで失敗する――これもまた転換点となる。: Attempting and failing to achieve the objective—this too becomes a turning point.
texts.例えば、物語中盤で宿敵に挑むが、返り討ちに合うような展開だ。: For example, the protagonists may challenge the archenemy midway through the story, only to be defeated.
texts.その後、宿敵を倒すための手段を探すといった展開に。: The story then develops into a search for a way to defeat the archenemy.
texts.あるいはその際に宿敵にヒロインをさらわれるなど、失敗の代償を払わされる展開にして: Alternatively, the failure could come at a cost, such as the archenemy abducting the heroine during the confrontation. The immediate objective then becomes rescuing the heroine.
texts.ＳＦなら「地球に衝突する隕石を阻止するためにロケット兵器を打ち上げるが、破壊に失: In science fiction, you could come up with ideas such as, “They launch a rocket weapon to stop a meteor from colliding with Earth, but fail to destroy it.”
texts.宿敵の正体は主人公の父だった！: The archenemy was the protagonist's father!
texts.敵を倒すためには、大きな犠牲を払う必要がある。: Defeating the enemy requires making a great sacrifice.
texts.上の例はＦＦ１０だが、「宿敵の正体」「倒すために必要な代償」などが掲示された結果: The example above is from Final Fantasy X, but once facts such as “the archenemy's identity” and “the sacrifice required to defeat them” are revealed, the significance of achieving the objective changes greatly for the protagonist. As a result, the protagonist also decides to change their means of achieving it.
texts.ただし、敵を倒すという目的自体は当初から変化していない。: However, the objective of defeating the enemy itself has not changed from the beginning.
texts.他にも「悪だと思っていた敵にも、同情できる事情があった」なんていう王道パターンも: Another classic example is when “even the enemy thought to be evil had circumstances that made them sympathetic.”
texts.さらに具体的に転を強調する方法を考えてみよう。: Let's consider some more specific ways to emphasize the turning point.
texts.『主人公側に関わるもの』『世界・舞台に関わるもの』の二種類に分けてみる。これらが: Let's divide them into two types: “things involving the protagonist's side” and “things involving the world and setting.” When these lead to “a change of objective,” they create an impactful turning point.
texts.『転』においては主人公側に関わる出来事が多用される傾向がある。: Events involving the protagonist's side tend to be used frequently in the “turning point” section.
texts.主人公やヒロイン、仲間に関わるイベントを起こすことで、印象的な転を作ろう。: Create an impactful turning point by introducing events involving the protagonist, heroine, or companions.
texts.主人公の変更。これはゲーム性への影響も大きな転換である。: Changing the protagonist. This is also a major shift that greatly affects the gameplay.
texts.王道なのは主人公が死亡するなどして、その子世代に主人公が変更されることだろう。こ: The classic example is for the protagonist to die or otherwise be replaced by their child in the next generation. This is often combined with the passage of time.
texts.単純なところでは、章が変わって視点となるキャラが交代するなど。ただし、それだけで: A simple example would be changing the point-of-view character when the chapter changes. However, that alone may be too weak to serve as a turning point.
texts.他にも主人公が危機的な状況に陥って、ヒロインなどの他のキャラが第二の主人公として: Another possibility is for the protagonist to fall into a critical situation, prompting another character, such as the heroine, to take action as a second protagonist.
texts.物語の流れを大きく変えるような主人公の決断。: A decision by the protagonist that dramatically changes the course of the story.
texts.所属組織からの脱退・離反: Leaving or defecting from their organization
texts.ストーリー上で強制しても良いし、もちろんプレイヤーに選択させてもよい。: You can force the decision as part of the story, or, of course, let the player choose.
texts.ＦＦ４の冒頭や、タクティクスオウガの一章終盤の選択肢などが有名だろう。: The opening of FF4 and the choice near the end of Chapter One in Tactics Ogre are famous examples.
texts.一時的にちょっと離脱するだけなら大したことはないが、死亡などの永久離脱は大きな衝: A brief, temporary departure is not a big deal, but a permanent departure, such as death, can be a major shock.
texts.時にはヒロインや主人公まで対象となったりする。: Sometimes even the heroine or protagonist can be affected.
texts.ＦＦ６のようにメンバー全員が離散するなんて展開も。: There are also developments like in FF6, where all the members are scattered.
texts.重要人物の裏切り: The Betrayal of an Important Character
texts.そのまま仲間だった人物が宿敵になったり、もう一度復縁したりと展開は様々。: The developments can vary: a former companion may become a sworn enemy, or the two may reconcile once again.
texts.重要人物の死亡: The Death of an Important Character
texts.例えば、パワーアップしたラスボスに師匠キャラが殺害されるような展開があれば、ラス: For example, if a mentor character is killed by a powered-up final boss, it will make the final boss more memorable.
texts.宿敵と思っていた相手が黒幕に殺されるとか、主人公に指示を出していた組織の長が殺さ: If the person you thought was your sworn enemy is killed by the mastermind, or the leader of the organization directing the protagonist is killed, the course of the story will change as well.
texts.当然、どうでもいいキャラでは転換点にはならない。: Naturally, the death of an insignificant character will not become a turning point.
texts.主人公やヒロインの秘密が明かされる: The Protagonist's or Heroine's Secret Is Revealed
texts.実は王族だったとか、人間じゃなかったとかいうのが最もベタだが、やりようはいくらで: The most clichéd examples are that they were actually royalty or were not human, but there are countless ways to handle it.
texts.それによって、新たな展開につながったりする。: This can lead to new developments.
texts.ネガティブな展開ばかりを書いている気がするけれど、ポジティブな展開も大事。: I feel like I've been writing only negative developments, but positive developments are important too.
texts.協力者の登場によって、絶望的な状況に光明が見えてくる展開など。: For example, the appearance of an ally can bring a glimmer of hope to a desperate situation.
texts.敵側の人物が改心して仲間になってくれるなども効果的だ。もしくは最初からスパイ的な: It can also be effective for someone on the enemy's side to repent and join the party. Another possibility is that they were actually an ally all along, merely pretending to act as a spy.
texts.例えば、主人公がヒロインに告白して成功する――なんて展開も場合によっては立派なタ: For example, the protagonist confessing their love to the heroine and succeeding can, in some cases, be a significant turning point.
texts.悪の組織に追われるヒロインを守る――といった動機づけによって、ストーリー展開に大: It can also have a major impact on the story's development by providing motivation such as protecting the heroine from an evil organization.
texts.中盤で結婚するＤＱ５なんかが有名。: DQ5, in which the protagonist gets married midway through the game, is a famous example.
texts.ただし、現代的な恋愛劇として見た場合は、圧倒的に描写が足りないのは玉に瑕。: However, when viewed as a modern romance, its regrettable flaw is that it lacks an overwhelming amount of character development.
texts.逆に振られてしまう場合も立派に印象づけられるけれど、いささかマニアックなのは否め: Being rejected can also make a strong impression, but I have to admit that it is somewhat niche, and the only famous example I know is that certain Lagoon game.
texts.世界・舞台に関わるもの: Things Involving the World and Setting
texts.物語の転換点においては、世界・舞台の変化が行われることも多い。: Story turning points are also often accompanied by changes to the world or setting.
texts.世界・舞台の移動: Moving to a Different World or Setting
texts.魔王が支配する暗黒の世界、雲の上の浮遊大陸、未知の生物が跋扈する地底……。こうい: A dark world ruled by a demon king, floating continents above the clouds, an underground realm teeming with unknown creatures... Moving to settings like these is one of the great pleasures of a large-scale RPG.
texts.ＳＦならば宇宙船で新たな惑星に移動したり、タイムマシンで別の時代に移動したりする: In science fiction, the characters may travel to a new planet by spaceship or to another era in a time machine.
texts.必ずしも、大規模な変化である必要はない。: The change does not necessarily have to be on a grand scale.
texts.ＦＦ７の序盤は、都市ミッドガルを舞台に物語が展開されるが、やがて世界を舞台にした: In the early part of FF7, the story unfolds in the city of Midgar, but eventually expands into a story set across the world. This is also a change of setting.
texts.時間経過によって、物語を転換させる手法。: A technique for shifting the story through the passage of time.
texts.有名なのはＤＱ５だろう。: DQ5 is probably the most famous example.
texts.父に連れられていた少年時代から、自ら立って歩く青年時代へと主人公は成長を遂げる。: The protagonist grows from a boy who was led around by his father into a young man who can stand and walk on his own.
texts.さらに再度の時間経過によって、誕生した子供達が成長して戦いに参加するようになる。: Then, after another passage of time, the children who were born grow up and join the battle.
texts.当然ながら、時間が経過すると世界中の住民も歳を取る。そういった住民の変化を実装す: Naturally, as time passes, the people throughout the world grow older as well. Implementing such changes among the inhabitants is quite a difficult task.
texts.そう考えると、序盤の多くの町が登場していない段階で、しかけるのが無難なところか。: With that in mind, it may be safest to introduce it before many towns appear in the early part of the story.
texts.実際、ごく序盤のイベントのみを少年期で行う作品も時々見かける。もっとも、これは『: In fact, I occasionally see works in which only the very early events take place during the protagonist's childhood. Still, this feels closer to the "setup" than the "turn."
texts.あるいは、一年程度の時間経過を導入する方法もある。: Alternatively, you could introduce a passage of about one year.
texts.こちらならば住民に大きな変化はないはずなので、セリフなどを変更しなくとも違和感は: Since the inhabitants should not change much in that time, it should not feel strange even if you do not change their dialogue.
texts.ただし、意味もなく時間経過を導入しても仕方ないので、何らかの変化は必要だが。: However, introducing a passage of time without a purpose would be pointless, so some kind of change is necessary.
texts.町や国が破壊されたり、島や大陸が沈んだりする。: Towns and countries are destroyed, or islands and continents sink beneath the sea.
texts.あるいはＦＦ６のように世界まるごと大打撃を受けてもよい。: Alternatively, the entire world could suffer a devastating blow, as in FF6.
texts.これによって敵の強大さや凶悪さを印象づけたり、主人公側に動機づけを行ったりする。: This can impress upon the player how powerful and ruthless the enemy is, or give the protagonist's side motivation to act.
texts.『起』でも『転』でも使えるイベント界の優等生。大規模にやると演出が大変になるのが: A model event that can be used for either the "setup" or the "turn." The drawback is that large-scale destruction can be difficult to stage.
texts.とりあえず主人公の故郷を焼いたりするのは基本。: Burning down the protagonist's hometown is a basic example.
texts.世界が暗闇に覆われる。雨が永遠に止まらない。世界中の陸地が水没する。モンスターの: The world is shrouded in darkness. The rain never stops. All the land in the world is submerged. Monsters appear in huge numbers. And so on…
texts.敵によって人為的に起こされたか、自然現象的なものなのかによって、また展開が変わっ: The story will develop differently depending on whether the enemy caused it deliberately or whether it is a natural phenomenon.
texts.隕石を阻止するＦＦ７のように、それら天変地異の阻止が最終目的となる場合もある。: In some cases, stopping such natural disasters becomes the ultimate goal, as in FF7, where the heroes must stop a meteor.
texts.「ラスボスを倒さないと世界がヤバい！」なんて文章を中心に説明する作品は多いけれど: Many works center their explanations around lines such as, "The world is doomed unless we defeat the final boss!" But that alone does not make the threat feel very real.
texts.上の『舞台の破壊』もそうだけど、こうやって具体的な演出を入れると効果てきめんだ。: The same applies to the "Destruction of the Setting" mentioned above, but adding concrete staging like this can be extremely effective.
texts.転の注意点: Points to Keep in Mind About the Turn
texts.ここまで熱烈に『転』を推してきたけど、転は万能ではない。強引に転をしかけた場合は: I have strongly advocated the "turn" up to this point, but it is not a cure-all. If you force a turn into the story, it can also have a negative effect.
texts.それはテーマがブレることである。: That effect is a shift in the theme.
texts.例えば「主人公とライバルとの対決」というテーマが物語の全体の多くを占める作品だっ: For example, suppose a work's overall story is largely devoted to the theme of "the protagonist's confrontation with their rival."
texts.そこで終盤になって唐突に「黒幕の手によって、ライバルが殺害される」という転を導入: What would happen if, near the end, you suddenly introduced a turn in which "the rival is killed by the mastermind"?
texts.これにより「主人公とライバルとの対決」というテーマが終わってしまうため、プレイヤ: This would bring the theme of "the protagonist's confrontation with their rival" to an end, so there is a high chance that players would lose interest.
texts.こういった場合も、なるべく自然なテーマの変化を目指そう。: Even in such cases, aim for the theme to change as naturally as possible.
texts.幾度の戦いの末、主人公とライバルはついに和解する。手段は違えど、二人とも世界の平: After countless battles, the protagonist and their rival finally reconcile. Although their methods differed, they shared the same aspiration to bring peace to the world.
texts.だが、ライバルを影で利用していた黒幕は彼を殺害する。: However, the mastermind who had been using the rival from the shadows kills him.
texts.世界征服を企む黒幕にとって、もはやライバルは邪魔でしかなかったのだ。: To the mastermind plotting to conquer the world, the rival was no longer anything but an obstacle.
texts.主人公はライバルの目指した世界平和を目指すため、黒幕との最後の戦いに挑む。: The protagonist challenges the mastermind to one final battle in order to pursue the world peace their rival had sought.
texts.テーマが「ライバルとの対決」から「ライバルの遺志を継ぐ」に転換されたわけだが、こ: The theme has shifted from "confronting the rival" to "carrying on the rival's will," which should feel relatively natural.
texts.以上、色々と例を挙げてみた。: Those are some of the various examples I could think of.
texts.簡単にできるものから演出的に難しいものまであるけれど、色々と考えてみていただけれ: Some are easy to implement, while others are difficult to stage, but I hope you will consider the possibilities.
texts.なお、実際には複数の要素を組み合わせて『転』を演出することが多い。: In practice, a "turn" is often created by combining multiple elements.
texts.例えば、ＦＦ６の中盤の転換点では、『目的の変化』『目的の難化』『目的の失敗』『舞: For example, the turning point in the middle of FF6 includes many elements, such as "a change in objectives," "an increasingly difficult objective," "failure to achieve the objective," "destruction of the setting," "the departure of a party member," and "the passage of time."
texts.強い印象を与えたい場合は、上述の要素を柔軟に組み合わせてみて欲しい。もちろん、こ: If you want to make a strong impression, try combining the elements mentioned above flexibly. Of course, there may also be effective methods among those not listed here.
